Pathogen Types: Viruses
• Very small – can only be seen with electron 
microscope.
• Contain genetic materials eg DNA/RNA, 
surrounded by protein coat.
• Enter cell and use their DNA/RNA to take 
over cell processes so virus can reproduce.
• Not all viruses are harmful/pathogenic – 
some are even used in biotechnology!
• Cannot be treated with antibiotics
• Vaccines available for some deadly viral 
diseases

Active Immunity 
•
 Body actively produces antibody 
•
 Antibody mediated process
•
 Memory cells produced
•
Long term immunity – more antibody can be 
produced each time pathogen is encountered.

Passive Immunity
•
Antibodies are gained from another source
•
Body gains antibody passively – immune system not 
involved.
•
No memory cells produced
•
Immunity only lasts until antibody used up.

Catching tetanus 
•
Tetanus toxin enters body, B-cells activated, 
antibody produced actively.
•
Immune system will recognise toxin next time 
it is encountered.

Getting tetanus antibodies from mothers’ milk
•
Antibodies will neutralise toxin if present but 
immune system isn’t activated, so no future 
immunity.

Getting the tetanus Vaccine
•
Tetanus toxoid vaccine enters body, B-cells 
activated, antibody produced actively.
•
Immune system will recognise toxin next time 
it is encountered.

Getting man-made tetanus antitoxin injected
•
Antibodies in antitoxin will neutralise toxin if present 
but immune system isn’t activated, so no future 
immunity.

Role in maintaining salt and water levels in body,

Acts on collecting ducts in kidney, causing 
increased Na+ and water reabsorption and 
increased K+ secretion.

Cortisol:

Role in response to stress, illness and metabolism
